title: Install a missing agent CLI on a Remote from the UI
body:
Let the user install a missing agent CLI on a Remote from the UI. Today Settings > Remotes > Test reports which agent CLIs (claude, codex, grok) and curl it found on the Remote (src/remote_probe.rs start_test, shown by src/remotes_pane.rs), and the launcher (src/launcher.rs entries_on) offers agents on a Remote whether or not they exist there. Add an install action for each agent CLI that Test reports missing.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (sections: UI > Settings > Remotes, Launch). Feature doc: docs/remote-sessions.md. Add a short "Installing an agent CLI" part to the spec's UI section describing what you build.
Blocked by: Design leftovers and the reply note on agent reconnect
Decided, do not reopen:
- The install runs VISIBLY, as an ordinary Remote Session (a shell on that Remote running the install command) opened through the existing WindowManager remote spawn path and remote::build. Never run an installer hidden in the background or from the probe thread: the user must see the output, answer any prompt (sudo, PATH, licence) and be able to Ctrl+C. The Session stays open when the command ends so the result can be read.
- It is always an explicit click or key on a named action. Nothing installs automatically, on Test, on launch, or on connect.
- Foreman installs nothing of its own on the Remote. "The other PC needs nothing from foreman" still holds: this only runs the vendor's own installer for the agent CLI. No foreman skills, hook files or helpers are copied there.
- Logging in is not part of this card. After an install the UI says the CLI still needs a login in a Session on that Remote.
Do:
1. One table (provider, shell kind) -> install command, in src/remote.rs beside RESUME, covering claude, codex and grok for Posix, and for Pwsh / WindowsPowerShell. Take each command from the vendor's current official install documentation; look it up, do not write it from memory, and put the source URL in a comment beside each entry. If a vendor has no official install command for a shell, leave that entry out; the UI then shows no install action for it and says to install it by hand. A command that needs a prerequisite (for example Node for an npm install) must be gated on Test having found that prerequisite; extend the Test probe to report it, and when it is missing show a plain message naming what is missing instead of an action that will fail.
2. Remotes pane: beside each agent CLI that the last Test reported missing, an "install" action in the same row-button style as test/edit/delete, with a keyboard path and a hint that fits one line at PANE_MIN_W. Before running, show the exact command and the Remote's name and ask to confirm (same confirm style as delete). On confirm, open the Remote Session in the focused Project (or say plainly that a Project must be open) and re-run Test when that Session exits, so the row updates.
3. Launcher: when a Remote is selected and its cached Test result says an agent CLI is missing, mark that agent row (dim plus a word, not colour alone) and make choosing it offer the same confirm-and-install instead of launching a command that will fail with "command not found". If the Remote has never been tested, the launcher behaves as today.
4. The curl prerequisite: the Tunnel reply needs curl on the Remote. If Test reports curl missing, say so in the same place; do not try to install OS packages.
Design bar (a designer reviews this from the code afterwards; earlier cards failed on these): theme tokens only; every state readable without colour alone (missing, installing, installed, needs a prerequisite, no install available); nothing shifts when a Test result arrives; long commands truncate with the full text on hover and in the confirm; copy is plain and names the Remote.
Not verified here, label it so: every Windows-Remote install command is untested (no Windows Remote exists). Grok is not installed on the test Remote andy@100.102.251.37 (key login, never ask for a password); do NOT run any installer against that machine yourself. Verifying a real install is for the human.
Done when:
- unit tests cover the install table (every entry has a command for its shell, a missing entry yields no action), the prerequisite gate, the pure model of the pane action and confirm, and the launcher model marking a missing agent; the launcher model with no Remotes is unchanged
- the install Session is spawned through the existing remote spawn path with the command as its logical argv (test on the argv, not by spawning)
- a layout test at PANE_MIN_W shows the install action and hint inside the pane
- the full test suite passes
- the final report lists the states the human should capture with build-screenshot and says which install commands were looked up where
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent
